title: Button visual variant (danger/success/accent) is recomputed three times in inline style
description: The inline `style` object computes the same branch selector for `background`, `border`, and `color`. Each of the three lines re-evaluates `(building && cancelFetchFn) || hasStatusError` and then `cache?.cached`, producing an identical 3-way variant decision triplicated across the properties. The variant should be computed once (e.g. `const variant = (building && cancelFetchFn) || hasStatusError ? 'danger' : cache?.cached ? 'success' : 'accent'`) and the three CSS-var lookups derived from it, removing the duplicated boolean ladder and making the danger/success/accent intent explicit.
evidence: Lines 224-226: `background: (building && cancelFetchFn) || hasStatusError ? 'var(--danger-soft)' : cache?.cached ? 'var(--success-soft)' : 'var(--accent-soft)'`, then the same `(building && cancelFetchFn) || hasStatusError ? ... : cache?.cached ? ...` ladder again for `border`, then again for `color`. Three evaluations of the same two predicates.
est_reduction: ~4 lines; removes 2 redundant evaluations of the variant predicate
behavior_preservation: Pure refactor: same CSS variables selected for the same state combinations; no change to rendered output.
